# Deferral Ledger

One line per deferral. Never close a task silently with a forward reference —
record what landed, what was deferred, and where to resume.

The `status` column tracks consumption of each deferral by milestone **M0119**
(see `docs/milestones/0119-deferral-ledger-backlog-consumption.md`). Values:
`-` = open / 未対応 (not yet consumed); `resolved` = the deferred scope has since
landed (by a later ledger row, a promotion, or current code) and has been
verified by an M0119 triage/consumption task. M0119 sets these values; appending
a new deferral row uses `-`.

Root cause: `recursiveUnionOp.Next()` fully drains one fixpoint iteration to EOF before returning any row to its caller, instead of real PG's row-at-a-time `nodeRecursiveunion.c` pull model (new rows are stored into the working-table tuplestore AND returned to the caller simultaneously) that lets an outer LIMIT stop the pull chain early even on a query graph that is not naturally finite. Here the inner `x`'s recursive term (`select * from q union all select * from x`) can never reach EOF on its own — draining it requires draining the still-open outer `q`, which (by the same rule) requires draining `x` — so the existing `maxRecursiveDepth` guard (which only advances between *completed* iterations) never fires; the process is stuck forever inside iteration one. The real fix needs (a) a row-at-a-time pull refactor of `recursiveUnionOp.Next()`/`Open()` so partial iteration results stream to the caller as produced, and (b) a shared/reentrant CTE-instance model across nested `WITH` scopes so `select * from q` inside `x`'s recursive term pulls from the SAME in-flight outer `q` computation rather than spinning up an independent second evaluation of `q` — both together are a real executor-core refactor, out of scope for a single M0134 loop. | `internal/executor/operators_recursive_cte.go` `recursiveUnionOp` — rework `Next()`'s Phase-2 loop into a state machine that keeps `o.recursive` open across `Next()` calls and returns each produced row immediately (still appending it to the pending `working` set for the next iteration), and separately design how a recursive CTE reference nested inside another recursive CTE's body resolves to the SAME running instance instead of a fresh operator subtree — likely needs a per-statement CTE-instance registry keyed by (query id, CTE name) threaded through `Context`, since `ctx.WorkTableRows`/`ctx.MaterializedCTEs` are currently keyed for the non-reentrant case. (3) **Range/multirange constructor functions are not callable.** `int4range`/`numrange`/etc. exist only as OID→name metadata (`internal/catalog/pg_proc_names_generated.go`) and as range-TYPE lookups (`catalog.LookupRangeType*`, `internal/executor/expr.go:19447-19500`) — no `evalFuncCall` dispatch case exists for calling them as functions (`grep "case \"int4range\""` in expr.go = empty), and there is no `multirange(...)` constructor at all; matches the diff's `ERROR: function int4range does not exist`. Root cause: goopg's range support is type-only with no Datum value model (per `expression_index_type_gate_test.go:29`'s own comment). (4) **`CREATE FUNCTION`-time polymorphic validation is missing** — PG rejects `RETURNS anycompatiblemultirange` with no polymorphic input to derive it from (`ERROR: cannot determine result data type`); goopg has no such check in `execCreateFunction`/`operators_ddl.go`, so the diff shows goopg either silently accepting the definition or erroring with an unrelated "function already exists" message on the `DROP`+`CREATE` re-run. (5) **`pg_statistic` base table is not registered as queryable**, only the derived `pg_stats` view is (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:9417-9441` registers `pg_stats`; `grep "Name: \"pg_statistic\""`/`grep "tables\[\"pg_catalog.pg_statistic\"\]"` both return nothing) even though a real per-database heap already exists at RelOid 2619 (written by `persistStatsToPGStatistic`, `internal/executor/operators_analyze.go:315-353`, `buildUserPGStatisticRow`, `internal/executor/pg18_user_catalog_rows.go:1531`) — `SELECT ... FROM pg_statistic` therefore fails `relation "pg_statistic" does not exist` even though the physical data is there; matches `internal/initdb/open.go:2795`'s existing `loadSystemCatalogsIfPresent` pattern for pg_type/pg_attribute (heap-file-present → `catalog.RegisterRealTable`) but that pattern is DefaultDBOid/startup-time-only and pg_statistic's heap is written per-connected-database on-demand by ANALYZE, so a straight port needs a per-DB dynamic registration, not a one-shot startup check. | (1) Add a real polymorphic-resolution pass ahead of `coerceDatumToType` in both `executeSQLRoutine` (`plpgsql_runtime.go:526`) and the PL/pgSQL routine path (`:1198` area), replicating PG's `resolve_polymorphic_argtypes`/`enforce_generic_type_consistency` (`postgres/src/backend/parser/parse_coerce.c`): unify `anyelement`/`anyarray`/`anynonarray`/`anyenum`/`anyrange`/`anymultirange` to one concrete family per call, and separately unify the whole `anycompatible*` family to a common supertype across possibly several differently-declared args (e.g. int + numeric → numeric); extend `resolveRoutineOverload` (`plpgsql_runtime.go:1021`) to do family-consistent overload matching instead of just deprioritizing polymorphic overloads. (2) SQL-function inlining is a separate large feature (planner-level body substitution + different error-CONTEXT/position reporting) with zero existing scaffolding — own milestone. (3) Range/multirange constructors need a new `Datum` range/multirange value representation plus new `evalFuncCall` cases (`internal/executor/expr.go`) for `int4range`/`numrange`/`daterange`/etc. and `multirange(...)` — a real value model, not just type metadata. (4) Add polymorphic-return-type validation to `execCreateFunction`/`operators_ddl.go` (reject a polymorphic RETURNS type with no corresponding polymorphic IN arg to derive it from). (5) `pg_statistic` registration: extend `loadSystemCatalogsIfPresent`'s pattern (`internal/initdb/open.go:2795`) to be per-connected-database rather than DefaultDBOid-only-at-startup — likely needs the same per-connection dynamic swap-in `fetchStatsRows` (`internal/executor/pgstat_tables.go:42`) already does for `pg_stats`, but backed by a real heap scan (`catalog.RegisterRealTable`-style) instead of a `VirtualRows` closure, since the pg_statistic heap is written lazily by ANALYZE per database. | Item 5 (`pg_statistic` registration) looked narrow at first glance (it directly explains the diff's first-line `relation "pg_statistic" does not exist` error) but investigation showed the existing pg_type/pg_attribute registration pattern is startup-time/DefaultDBOid-only while pg_statistic's heap is written lazily per connected database by ANALYZE — a correct fix needs the same per-connection dynamic-registration machinery `pg_stats`/`fetchStatsRows` uses, which is real but non-trivial cross-cutting work (per-connection virtual-catalog scoping, `per_connection_virtual_catalog_scoping` memory), not a same-pattern copy-paste; landing a half-correct version (e.g. DefaultDBOid-only) risked a silent wrong-database gap under time pressure. Items 1-4 are independently subsystem-scale (polymorphic-type unification, SQL inlining, range value model, CREATE-FUNCTION-time validation) with no existing narrow extension point beyond the already-tiny/wrong 2-of-11-pseudo-type `resolvePolymorphicReturnType`. Recommend polymorphism.sql become its own dedicated milestone (candidate name: "polymorphic function type resolution") rather than attempting a fragment here — consistent with how M0134 has already spun off dedicated-milestone recommendations for GiST/SPGiST plan integration, pg_shdepend/CASCADE, and the Large Object facility. |
